html:
In 1578 the Mongol ruler Altan Khan gave the Tibetan monk Sonam Gyatso the title Dalai Lama. The two met near Lake Kokonor, where Sonam Gyatso taught the khan.

Dalai is Mongolian for "ocean", a translation of Gyatso. Sonam Gyatso led the Gelug school, and the title was given back in time to two earlier heads of his line, so he counted as the third Dalai Lama.

The deal bound Tibetan Buddhism to the Mongols. Altan Khan gained religious standing for his rule, and the Gelug school gained a strong patron. Mongol nobles turned to Buddhism in large numbers. The fourth Dalai Lama was found in Altan Khan's own family. With Mongol troops the fifth became ruler of Tibet in 1642, and the line runs to the fourteenth today.
sum: In 1578 the Mongol ruler Altan Khan gave the Tibetan monk Sonam Gyatso the title Dalai Lama. The two met near Lake Kokonor, where Sonam Gyatso taught the khan.
